- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., 60+), often overshooting by 5–15% and failing to correct downward.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast (days 10–20), failing to capture upward momentum.
- Underreacts to recent high prices; fails to mean-revert toward historical averages when prices are above 65.
- Lags in recognizing price reversals; often forecasts a continuation of a downtrend after a bottoming point.
- Overly optimistic in late forecast days (days 25–30), especially when true prices are rising sharply (e.g., 70+).
- Tends to smooth out volatility; underweights recent price spikes and overweights prior trends.
